abstract: Cellular senescence remodels the microenvironment via SASP, and immune inflammation promotes carcinogenesis through DNA damage and immune remodeling; the “senescence-inflammation” vicious cycle formed by these two processes is a core driver of cancer development and progression, yet its mechanism in prostate cancer progression remains unclear. title: Targeting neuroinflammation in diabetic peripheral neuropathy: Mechanistic perspectives, phytochemical pharmacology, and translational challenges.
abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a debilitating neurodegenerative complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by the convergence of metabolic dysregulation, microvascular ischemia, and chronic low-grade neuroinflammation. While intensive glycemic control and cardiometabolic risk-factor modification slow neuropathy progression-most notably in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM)-approved central analgesic pharmacotherapies primarily manage nociceptive symptoms without directly reversing established structural axonal loss. Investigational phytochemicals, including curcumin, resveratrol, berberine, and quercetin, modulate these inflammatory and oxidative nodes in experimental rodent models. abstract: Quercetin could induce changes to the fluid volume and receptivity development of the uterus during peri-implantation period. In another cohort of rats, implantation rate was determined at day-6 (following five days quercetin treatment). Administration of 50mg/kg/day quercetin causes increased in uterine fluid volume and CFTR expression but decreased in γ-ENaC, AQP-5, AQP-9 claudin-4, occludin, E-cadherin, integrin αnβЗ, FGF, Ihh and Msx-1expression in the uterus. Pinopodes were poorly develop, tight junctions appear less complex and implantation rate decreased. Serum estradiol levels increased but serum progesterone levels decreased. Interference in the fluid volume and receptivity development of the uterus during peri-implantation period by quercetin could adversely affect embryo implantation.

title: Oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembled nanoparticles alleviate neurological injury after ischemic stroke via the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β axis.
abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability, while the current clinically applicable adjunctive neuroprotective strategies face substantial limitations. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin exhibit synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities; however, their poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability remain major limitations to their therapeutic development. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin were formulated as co-assembled nanoparticles using an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. A 5:2 mass ratio of oleanolic acid to hesperetin produced primarily spherical nanoparticles with a mean hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 282.6 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.197, and a zeta potential of -12.2 mV. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles displayed minimal hemolysis (0.199%) while maintaining a stable hydrodynamic diameter during 30 days of storage. Spectroscopic analyses and a 50 ns molecular dynamics simulation promoted co-assembly via multiple noncovalent-driven interactions. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles effectively reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced viability loss and apoptosis in HT22 cells.

title: Dietary Citrus Flavonoid Hesperetin Attenuates Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease via Modulation of MAPK-RARα Axis.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) lacks effective nutrition-based interventions. Hesperetin, a dietary citrus flavonoid, was evaluated for its hepatoprotective mechanism using high-fat diet-induced MASLD mice and free fatty acid-challenged hepatocytes. Hesperetin improved glucose and lipid metabolism, alleviated steatosis and inflammation, and restored hepatic function. Integrated transcriptomics and network analysis indicated activation of retinol metabolism and inhibition of MAPK signaling. Mechanistic studies showed that hesperetin suppressed aberrant MAPK activity, preserved retinoic acid receptor α (RARα) function, upregulated RARα-dependent metabolic genes, and reduced lipogenic gene expression. Pharmacological blockade or siRNA knockdown of RARα abrogated hesperetin's lipid-lowering effects, confirming RARα as an essential mediator. These findings identify hesperetin as a food-derived modulator of the MAPK-RARα axis that restores retinoid signaling and ameliorates hepatic lipid dysregulation, highlighting its potential as a targeted nutritional strategy for MASLD management.

title: Oral consumption of α-glucosyl-hesperidin could prevent lens hardening, which causes presbyopia.
abstract: Presbyopia is one of the most well-known diseases of the eye, predominantly affecting the adult population after 50 years'. Due to hardening of the lens and failure of accommodative change, patients lose the ability to focus on near objects. This eye symptom is reported to be an early symptom of age-related nuclear cataract, and we have previously reported that hesperetin treatment could delay the onset of nuclear cataractogenesis induced by sodium selenite. In this study, we examined whether oral intake of α-glucosyl-hesperidin (G-Hsd), which has greater water solubility than hesperetin, could delay the onset of presbyopia. abstract: Porcine circovirus 3 (PCV3) is a prevalent swine pathogen that causes multiple clinical disorders and threatens the global pig industry. abstract: Bradyarrhythmia is a prevalent cardiac disorder often necessitating lifelong pacemaker implantation, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study investigated the role of Peroxiredoxin 3 (PRDX3), a mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme, in the pathogenesis of bradyarrhythmia. A rat model of bradyarrhythmia was constructed.  We observed a significant downregulation of PRDX3 in the cardiac ganglion plexus (CGP) in bradyarrhythmia rats. PRDX3 knockdown in primary CGP cells exhibited hallmark features of ferroptosis, including iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, PRDX3 deficiency led to excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which inactivated the glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) signaling pathway, thereby driving ferroptotic cell death. Restoration of PRDX3 expression  Our findings demonstrate that PRDX3 downregulation promotes bradyarrhythmia progression via inducing ferroptosis and inflammatory M1 macrophage infiltration, revealing a novel role of PRDX3 in bradyarrhythmia.

title: Upregulation of PGC-1α attenuates obesity-exacerbated myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by restoring mitochondrial dynamics.
abstract: Compared to normal individuals, obese individuals demonstrate exacerbated myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury and higher mortality, despite comparable baseline cardiac function. The underlying mechanisms may involve obesity-induced pathophysiological changes-particularly energy metabolism dysregulation and mitochondrial dysfunction-which impair the ability of cardiomyocytes to withstand I/R injury, thereby increasing myocardial susceptibility. Mitochondria, serving as the central hub of energy metabolism, are critically regulated by peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α), a master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic homeostasis. However, the role of PGC-1α in the increased susceptibility of obese myocardium to I/R injury remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which obesity exacerbates myocardial vulnerability to I/R injury, with a specific focus on the role of PGC-1α and mitochondrial dysfunction, to facilitate the development of innovative therapeutic strategies for mitigating I/R injury and improving clinical outcomes in obese patients. Current treatment methods for osteoporosis do not fully restore bone quality and cause many side effects. The use of phytomolecules in combination with conventional treatment, in a time-sensitive manner aligned with circadian biology, is expected to be a better treatment for osteoporosis. title: Oleanolic acid-hesperetin co-assembled nanoparticles alleviate neurological injury after ischemic stroke via the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β axis.
abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability, while the current clinically applicable adjunctive neuroprotective strategies face substantial limitations. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin exhibit synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities; however, their poor aqueous solubility and limited bioavailability remain major limitations to their therapeutic development. Oleanolic acid and hesperetin were formulated as co-assembled nanoparticles using an emulsion-solvent evaporation method. A 5:2 mass ratio of oleanolic acid to hesperetin produced primarily spherical nanoparticles with a mean hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 282.6 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.197, and a zeta potential of -12.2 mV. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles displayed minimal hemolysis (0.199%) while maintaining a stable hydrodynamic diameter during 30 days of storage. Spectroscopic analyses and a 50 ns molecular dynamics simulation promoted co-assembly via multiple noncovalent-driven interactions. Oleanolic acid-hesperetin nanoparticles effectively reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion-induced viability loss and apoptosis in HT22 cells.

title: Myricetin inhibits porcine circovirus 3 infection by targeting the viral capsid and modulating inflammatory and apoptotic pathways.
abstract: Porcine circovirus 3 (PCV3) is a prevalent swine pathogen that causes multiple clinical disorders and threatens the global pig industry. This study explored the anti-PCV3 activity and underlying mechanisms of myricetin, a natural flavonoid, in porcine kidney 15 (PK-15) cells. Results showed that myricetin suppressed PCV3 replication in a dose- and time-dependent manner, primarily by interfering with viral attachment and early entry. Molecular docking indicated myricetin binding to the PCV3 capsid. Further Western blotting validation revealed that myricetin also activated the Akt and ERK cascades, remodeled JAK-STAT signaling, and relieved PCV3-induced excessive autophagy and mitochondrial apoptosis. Network pharmacology screened six core host targets involved in the cell cycle, inflammation, autophagy, and apoptosis. Collectively, myricetin exhibited anti-PCV3 activity by targeting the viral capsid and regulating multiple host signaling pathways. This work provides experimental evidence for the development of myricetin as a promising natural agent against PCV3 infection.

title: Response surface optimisation of Xiaoyao San polyphenols and anti-inflammatory activity in colonic epithelial cells.
abstract: Xiaoyao San is a traditional Chinese medicine formula, but its polyphenol extraction and intestinal epithelial activity remain insufficiently defined. We optimised ethanol-reflux extraction by response surface methodology and evaluated the polyphenol-rich fraction in NCM460 cells. The validated optimum was 57% ethanol, a 7.6 mL/g liquid-solid ratio, and 94 min, yielding 7.44 ± 0.15 mg gallic acid equivalents per gram. Xiaoyao San increased cell viability and proliferation, reduced apoptosis and nitrite accumulation, and decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 concentrations. title: Modulation of redox homeostasis, inflammation and endoplasmic reticulum stress mediate the protective effect of nifuroxazide against bisphenol A-induced kidney injury.
abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is an environmental toxicant known to impair kidney structure and function through oxidative and inflammatory pathways. Nifuroxazide (NFZ), an antidiarrheal agent with reported antioxidant and immunomodulatory potential, was evaluated for its ability to counteract BPA nephrotoxicity, focusing on redox imbalance, inflammation and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Adult male rats were administered BPA and/or NFZ orally for 28 days. BPA administration resulted in marked renal dysfunction, evidenced by elevated serum creatinine, BUN, uric acid, and Kim-1, along with histopathological deterioration and collagen accumulation. BPA increased lipid peroxidation and upregulated NF-κB p65, TNF-α, and IL-1β, and decreased GSH, SOD, catalase, and IL-10. Moreover, BPA triggered ER stress and apoptosis as reflected by increased expression of CHOP, GRP78, GRP75, and cleaved caspase-3.
